source_text.body:
Split Claude Code into a multi-agent dev team
A developer set up 12 specialized subagents for a React project, covering coding, review, debugging, refactoring and git commits, with the main session dispatching tasks.
·
Nov 17, 2026
Done with
CC
Claude Code
What they did
Each subagent is a markdown file in ~/.claude/agents/ with its own prompt, tools and model. Prompts embed the project's code patterns. The main session routes work using each agent's description: architect, types, senior-dev builds bottom-up, read-only reviewer, then a Haiku git agent commits. Independent steps can run in parallel.
How it went
The author says features now follow consistent patterns and reviews catch violations automatically. The source gives no measurements, and the author calls the setup a work in progress.
Try it yourself
with
Claude Code
Copy prompt
Set up a team of specialized subagents for my [framework] project at [repo path], covering coding, code review, debugging, refactoring, and git commits. Write each as a subagent file with a clear description so the main session knows when to delegate. Finish by running one small real task through the team and summarizing which agents handled which parts.
Original source: https://dev.to/matkarimov099/how-i-split-claude-code-into-12-specialized-sub-agents-for-my-react-project-3jh8
